set.body:
Outcome

Eliminate Scala Array staging and private flat-order conventions from image computation while making every kernel layout requirement explicit.

Work

- Inventory every output Array, fromLinear call, flat ordinal loop, copied matrix conversion, slice copy, map, zip, reduction, stencil, transform, and resampling path.
- Construct immutable outputs with NDArray.build or authoritative Ravel kernels so one output buffer is allocated and retained.
- Classify kernels as general view-safe, whole-canonical, or explicitly workload-prepared.
- Move generic traversal, elementwise, reduction, and stencil machinery to Ravel, and generic resampling execution to reframe4s; retain neuroimaging policy in ScalaFIM.
- Provide separate view and materialized APIs where a zero-copy result is not always possible.
- Keep mutable scratch internal, bounded, primitive, and allocation-accounted.

Acceptance

- Production image algorithms no longer allocate a full Scala Array merely to copy it into Ravel.
- Hot paths state and test layout prerequisites instead of silently canonicalizing per call or per access.
- Allocation receipts prove one destination for representative map, zip, reduction, resampling, searchlight, and dense or sparse conversions.
- View and whole-canonical numerical oracles agree on asymmetric inputs.
- Focused image, spatial, motion, threshold, atlas, and MVPA suites pass on JVM and Scala.js.
set.title: Move image algorithms and transformations to view-aware Ravel builders and kernels
